title: Fair Column Subset Selection

problem.claim: Select a subset of columns from an input matrix that minimizes the maximum reconstruction error for two row groups relative to their respective best rank-k approximations.

gap.claim: Extending column subset selection to the fair two-group setting is not straightforward because some scenarios require selecting columns separately for each group, potentially doubling the expected column count.

contributions.claim: A deterministic leverage-score sampling strategy is proposed for fair column subset selection.
The minimum-size fair column subset problem is shown to be NP-hard when there are two groups, and an approximation algorithm with solution size at most 1.5 times optimal is provided.
Practical heuristic algorithms based on rank-revealing QR factorization are presented.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validating their methods through an extensive set of experiments on real-world data.

narrative_sequence.summary: Column subset selection reconstructs a matrix using the span of selected columns.
The fair setting partitions rows into two groups and controls the worst relative reconstruction error across groups.
Fair selection can require separate columns for each group, increasing the expected column count.
The work introduces leverage-score sampling, establishes NP-hardness, gives a 1.5-approximation, and presents QR-based heuristics.
The methods are evaluated on real-world data.

source_observation.claim: Fairness is formulated as controlling the maximum reconstruction error across groups relative to group-specific rank-k benchmarks.

interpretation.claim: A shared representation can be assessed by its worst-group approximation quality rather than only by aggregate error.

application.claim: For grouped matrix-representation tasks, compare shared feature subsets using worst-group relative reconstruction error.

exception.claim: Some settings may require separate group-specific selections, increasing the number of selected columns.
